biology.cells-describe.0003.all: Stem cells (embryonic/adult) are undifferentiated; treated/stimulated to differentiate into nerve cells; transplanted/injected into damaged area to replace damaged cells; use patient's own cells to avoid rejection

biology.cells-describe-multi.0004.b: Chloroplast: oval, contains stacks/grana/green, larger; mitochondrion: smaller, folded inner membrane (cristae)

biology.cells-explain.0007.all: Enzymes are proteins; ribosomes are site of protein synthesis so many ribosomes make large amounts of protein

biology.cells-explain-multi.0002.a: Process by which a cell becomes specialised for a particular function
biology.cells-explain-multi.0002.b: Water enters both by osmosis; plant cell has cell wall which is strong/rigid and resists expansion so cell becomes turgid; animal cell has no cell wall so membrane bursts (lysis)

biology.cells-ext.0008.all: Benefits: stem cells can differentiate into heart muscle cells, replace damaged tissue, restore function, avoid transplant waiting/rejection if own cells. Problems: embryonic ethical issues, rejection by immune system, risk of uncontrolled division/tumours, infection/viral transfer, expensive, uncertain success

biology.cells-mcq-rev.0001.all: Contains the genetic material that controls the activities of the cell

biology.cells-recall.0001.all: A group of similar cells working together to carry out a particular function

biology.cells-recall-multi.0004.a: Process by which cells become specialised

biology.characteristics-explain.0003.all: Metabolic reactions produce waste products (e.g. CO2, urea); these are toxic and would build up/poison cells if not removed

biology.characteristics-explain-multi.00.b: Enzymes work best within narrow range of temperature/pH; to keep cells/reactions working properly / prevent damage to cells (e.g. osmosis)

biology.characteristics-mcq-rev.0001.all: Involves taking in or making the food an organism needs

biology.cloning-describe.0004.all: Many plants produced quickly; in small space; all genetically identical with desired features; can be done any time of year; disease-free plants

biology.cloning-describe-multi.0004.b: Small pieces (explants) cut from parent tip; sterilised; placed on agar with nutrients and hormones (auxin); grow into small plantlets; transferred to compost; aseptic conditions

biology.cloning-explain.0003.all: Genetic material/DNA is in the nucleus; lamb's nucleus came from donor so it has donor's genes/alleles; surrogate contributed no DNA

biology.cloning-explain-multi.0004.b: Nucleus contains the genes; donor nucleus so genetically identical to donor; surrogate gives no genes

biology.cloning-mcq.0004.all: every clone carries the human gene and makes the protein

biology.cloning-mcq-rev.0003.all: Carries a cloned embryo to birth
